title: Modern Control Flow & Deferrable Views
exp: Angular 17+ control flow (@if, @for, @switch) and @defer blocks revolutionize template performance and lazy loading.
pts: **`@if / @else` & `@switch`:** native template control flow syntax replacing `*ngIf` and `*ngSwitch`.
**`@for (item of items; track item.id)`:** mandatory `track` expression for optimal DOM reuse without `trackBy` boilerplate.
**`@defer (on viewport; prefetch on idle)`:** deferred loading of heavy components, automatically generating separate JS bundles.
**`@placeholder`, `@loading`, `@error`** blocks for smooth deferred UI loading states.
pr: Add @defer with placeholder skeletons to a heavy dashboard component

qa.q: Why is the `track` expression mandatory in `@for` loops?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Mandatory track forces developers to provide a unique key for DOM node identity, ensuring Angular reuses existing DOM elements on array mutation rather than destroying and recreating the entire DOM sub-tree.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Operating Why is the `track` expression mandatory in `@for` loops? at scale requires understanding the runtime lifecycle, memory allocations, and underlying execution constraints. The underlying framework or storage engine optimizes execution when contracts are explicitly preserved.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Un-handled edge cases in Why is the `track` expression mandatory in `@for` loops? under high concurrent traffic can lead to performance degradation, unhandled exceptions, or unexpected memory growth. Always enforce defensive validation and error handling.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Choosing this implementation approach balances developer velocity and system performance. Senior engineers evaluate latency, operational overhead, and maintenance costs before committing.

qa.q: Explain how `@defer (on viewport)` improves Initial Page Load (Core Web Vitals).
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Components inside @defer are code-split into separate bundle chunks and not downloaded or compiled until the deferred DOM container scrolls into the browser viewport, lowering initial JavaScript bundle execution time.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** EF Core builds an Expression Tree, translates it via the relational SQL provider into a parameterized T-SQL query, and materializes entities into the DbContext Change Tracker. N+1 queries occur when navigating un-included navigation properties in a loop.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Executing queries without AsNoTracking() in read-only APIs forces EF Core to keep snapshot copies of all returned entities in memory, causing high RAM usage and CPU tracking overhead.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** AsNoTracking() speeds up read queries by 20-30% and reduces memory footprint, but disables identity resolution and automatic change tracking for updates.
